properties.name: Advait Waterfall
properties.summary: Vangan's neighbour fall on the Dang–Navsari line — Advait drops a kilometre from the Ankada Dhodh, doubling the Vansda-side outing.

properties.name: Anjan Kund (Anjani Parvat)
properties.summary: A forest kund and cave on Anjani hill held locally as Hanuman's birthplace — a short trek into Dang's Ramayana geography.

properties.name: Artist Village (Gandharvapur)
properties.summary: A working craft centre outside Saputara where Warli painting and bamboo work are made, taught and sold by the artists themselves.

properties.name: Baaj Waterfall
properties.summary: Baaj village's falls and ridge-top view point on the Waghai side — a fall, a vista and, close by, the Koshmal forest country in one stop.

properties.name: Barda Falls
properties.summary: A little-documented interior-Dang monsoon waterfall near Barda village — for completists willing to ask directions and accept a rough approach.

properties.name: Bhalkhet Waterfall
properties.summary: A monsoon waterfall in the Godadiya village country of Subir taluka — a local-crowd trekking spot west of the Girmal belt.

properties.name: Bhambhi Waterfall
properties.summary: A forest waterfall in Dang's far east by the Maharashtra border — a trekkers' find beyond Ahwa that the vlogs rate among the district's prettiest.

properties.name: Birsa Waterfall
properties.summary: A reels-famous forest cascade between Ahwa and Don — a waterfall that exists mostly as a map pin, monsoon videos and word of mouth.

properties.name: Chikhalda Waterfall
properties.summary: The anchor fall of Dang's south-western pocket — Chikhalda drops by its village, with the Vadla ni vadi banyan grove beside the approach.

properties.name: Chimer (Chichkund) Falls
properties.summary: Four cascades off a ~100 m escarpment on Dang's northern rim — locally claimed as Gujarat's tallest waterfall, and almost entirely unvisited.

properties.name: Chirai Waterfalls
properties.summary: The far corner of the Waghai-side falls country — Chirai drops in the forest toward the Vansda border, the loop's last and loneliest stop.

properties.name: Dev Van Waterfall
properties.summary: The falls reels call 'Wonder Waterfall' — Dev Van's monsoon drop in the Subir forest belt, a short forest walk from the Godadiya country roads.

properties.name: Dhulda Waterfall
properties.summary: A village waterfall west of the Girmal country — Dhulda rounds out the Subir belt's falls cluster on the quiet side of the forest roads.

properties.name: Don Waterfall
properties.summary: Don village's own monsoon waterfall — a 1–2 km walk to a pool-bottomed drop, with changing rooms at the base and a genuinely rough approach road.

properties.name: Don Hill Station
properties.summary: A quiet tribal village on one of Gujarat's highest plateaus — grass meadows, ridge walks and valley views without Saputara's crowds.

properties.name: Echo Point
properties.summary: A curve on Saputara's rim road where the facing cliffs bounce a clean echo — a five-minute stop kids refuse to leave.

properties.name: Gaumukh Waterfalls (Songadh)
properties.summary: A seasonal forest waterfall with a small Gaumukh temple, ~15 km from Songadh just over the Dang–Tapi line — rugged approach, monsoon-only flow.

properties.name: Gira Falls
properties.summary: Dang's most visited waterfall — a broad ~23 m (75 ft) curtain near Waghai that turns thunderous after the June rains and runs through early winter.

properties.name: Girmal Falls
properties.summary: Gujarat's tallest waterfall — a roughly 30 m plunge on the Gira river deep in interior Dang, thundering from July to October.

properties.name: Governor's Hill
properties.summary: A wooded knoll above Saputara town with walking paths and quiet town-and-valley views — the low-key alternative to the headline points.

properties.name: Hatgadh Fort
properties.summary: A hill fort just across the Maharashtra border from Saputara — an hour's rocky climb to ramparts, rock-cut cisterns and huge two-state views.

properties.name: Honey Bee Centre
properties.summary: Saputara's little apiculture stop — hive demonstrations, bee lore and forest honey to take home; check it's operating before you plan around it.

properties.name: Janki Van
properties.summary: A Ramayana-themed forest garden at Bhinar near Unai — ten sacred groves, a tribal hut and tens of thousands of trees where Sita is said to have stayed.

properties.name: Kadam Dungar
properties.summary: An 800-metre hill off the Ahwa–Waghai road — one of Dang's high points, sacred to the Adivasi villages around it, with sunset views over the whole belt.

properties.name: Kaka-Kaki Waterfall
properties.summary: A three-step fall of 200-plus feet on the Gujarat–Maharashtra border forest near Gusrangam — among south Gujarat's tallest, and its least visited.

properties.name: Kilad Nature Education Campsite
properties.summary: Forest-department campsite on the Ambika river near Waghai — riverside cottages, nature trails and an easy first taste of Dang's forests.

properties.name: Koshmal Falls (Bhigu Dhodh)
properties.summary: The Waghai belt's secret — a forceful monsoon fall past Dungarda village, where a local guide is essential and the forest department posts warnings.

properties.name: Kunda Waterfall
properties.summary: Ahwa's own waterfall — Kunda drops in the forest edge barely six kilometres south of the district headquarters, the town's quick monsoon fix.

properties.name: Lake Garden
properties.summary: Lawns, play corners and shaded benches right on Saputara Lake's shore — the default family unwind after boating.

properties.name: Mahal Eco Campsite
properties.summary: Forest-department cottages on the Purna river deep inside Purna sanctuary — the base for dawn walks, river mornings and real forest nights.

properties.name: Karanjwa Waterfall
properties.summary: Karanjwa — the falls the Mahal-campsite crowd calls 'Mahal waterfall' — a monsoon drop in the Subir belt between the Girmal country and Bhalkhet.

properties.name: Maharaychond Forest
properties.summary: A picnic forest in the village country south of Ahwa — shade, birdsong and spread-a-mat ground on the Wasurna side of the district.

properties.name: Mayadevi Temple
properties.summary: A Devi shrine in Dang's north-western forest country — quiet most of the year, a living centre of the district's adivasi devotion on its fair days.

properties.name: Medha Waterfall
properties.summary: A multi-tiered cascade in the Songadh forests near Jamkhadi — a 15–20 minute jungle trek, free entry, and locals call it Gujarat's Dudhsagar.

properties.name: Milan Waterfall
properties.summary: The Subir belt's third falls — Milan sits between Bhalkhet and Dev Van, a monsoon drop the web never documented until its map pin surfaced.

properties.name: Nageshwar Mahadev Temple
properties.summary: Lakeside Shiva temple woven into Saputara's serpent-worship roots — small, active, and busiest during Shravan and festival evenings.

properties.name: Padam Dungari Eco Campsite
properties.summary: Forest-department campsite on the Ambika river in the hills near Vyara — riverside cottages and trails that pair with the Waghai belt.

properties.name: Pampa Sarovar
properties.summary: A quiet sacred pond near Subir tied to the Shabari story — forest-edged water, small shrines and almost no crowd.

properties.name: Pandav Caves & Waterfall
properties.summary: A cave shrine of Pandava exile lore with a monsoon waterfall beside it — reached by a rough 1.5–3 km trek from Javatla village off the Ahwa road.

properties.name: Pilva Dungar
properties.summary: 'The last hill of Gujarat' at Chorvani near Vansda — a monsoon-green dungar with the Pindhara Dev shrine, loved by trekkers and off-roaders alike.

properties.name: Purna Wildlife Sanctuary
properties.summary: Dense teak-and-bamboo forest on the Purna river — one of Gujarat's rainiest tracts, with forest drives, trails and the Mahal campsite at its heart.

properties.name: Pushpak Ropeway
properties.summary: Saputara's cable car glides from the lake side across the valley to the Sunset Point ridge — ten scenic minutes each way.

properties.name: Raja Rani Waterfall
properties.summary: Twin jungle falls deep in Purna sanctuary — Raja and Rani drop within sight of each other, earned by a proper monsoon forest trek.

properties.name: Ritu Waterfall
properties.summary: Chikhalda's kilometre-away sibling in the south-western pocket — a second small monsoon drop for the same village outing.

properties.name: Rose Garden
properties.summary: Saputara's rose beds near the lakefront — modest in size, at their fragrant best on cool winter mornings.

properties.name: Rupgadh Fort
properties.summary: Hilltop fort remains linked to Dang's Bhil kings — a forest trek to ramparts few tourists have ever heard of.

properties.name: Saputara Adventure Park
properties.summary: Operator-run adventure activities on Governor's Hill — ziplines, rope courses, ATVs; seasonal and variable, so confirm before promising the kids.

properties.name: Saputara Lake
properties.summary: Saputara's centrepiece — a calm hilltop lake with pedal and row boating, garden-lined banks, and the town's liveliest evening scene.

properties.name: Saputara Tribal Museum
properties.summary: Compact museum of Dangi life — masks, instruments, house models and household tools that decode the villages you drive past in Dang.

properties.name: Shabari Dham
properties.summary: Hilltop temple near Subir marking the spot where, by local tradition, Shabari offered wild berries to Ram — a key Ramayana site in Dang.

properties.name: Shivghat
properties.summary: A riverside Shiva shrine and bathing ghat on the Ahwa–Saputara road — a shady halt where road, river and a small temple meet.

properties.name: Songadh Fort
properties.summary: The Gaekwads' first hill stronghold above Songadh town — gate, ramparts and long Tapi-country views up a short stepped climb from the bazaar.

properties.name: Soul to Prakriti Waterfall
properties.summary: A forest fall two kilometres from Medha's cascades on the Dang–Tapi line — the border belt's quiet extra drop, name and all.

properties.name: Step Garden
properties.summary: Terraced hillside garden in Saputara town — planted steps, shaded corners and short winding paths that suit an easy family hour.

properties.name: Sunrise Point (Valley View Point)
properties.summary: East-facing viewpoint a short drive from Saputara town where the valley fills with dawn mist — the quiet counterpart to Sunset Point.

properties.name: Sunset Point (Gandhi Shikhar)
properties.summary: Saputara's classic evening ritual — a west-facing ridge reached by ropeway or a stepped climb, with layered Sahyadri views at dusk.

properties.name: Svtis Waterfall
properties.summary: Svtis waterfall between the Wasurna valley and the Chikhalda pocket — a small monsoon drop that extends the south-western loop by one stop.

properties.name: Table Point
properties.summary: A flat hilltop meadow on Saputara's rim with wide valley views, pony rides and snack stalls — the easiest family stop in town.

properties.name: Temburgartha Dam
properties.summary: A small dam and reservoir ten kilometres south of Ahwa — evening water views, and the ridge beside it doubles as the local sunset (and phone-signal) point.

properties.name: Town View Point
properties.summary: A roadside rise overlooking Saputara's rooftops, lake and plateau bowl — the postcard-of-the-town shot in one stop.

properties.name: U Turn Eco Tourism Point
properties.summary: The forest-department deck above the Gira river's full hairpin bend on the Girmal approach — the interior drive's classic tea-and-view halt.

properties.name: Unai Mata Temple & Hot Springs
properties.summary: The hot-spring temple of Ushnamba Mata at Unai — Rama's arrow raised the boiling kund in the telling, and pilgrims have bathed in it ever since.

properties.name: Valley of Wasurna
properties.summary: A valley vista in the village country south of Ahwa — green bowls, field terraces and forest ridges where almost nobody stops.

properties.name: Vangan Waterfall (Ankada Dhodh)
properties.summary: The Ankada Dhodh at Vangan village near Vansda — a vlog-discovered border fall, with the Gandavle hill viewpoint above the same village.

properties.name: Vansda National Park
properties.summary: A compact national park of dense old forest bordering Waghai — giant squirrels, pythons, leopards and butterflies in barely 24 km².

properties.name: Waghai Botanical Garden
properties.summary: A large forest-department botanical campus at Waghai — labelled native trees, bamboo groves and shaded walks at the foot of the Dang hills.
